note: Statements of Persons Nominated transcribed by reading the newspaper scans DIRECTLY, notice by notice, rather than by OCR. This supersedes archive/ocr/ for every file listed here. Review material: not used by the build or the site, and nothing here is published.
why: Two OCR passes and an LLM extraction all damaged this material, and the damage was not visible from inside the pipeline. Reading the scans is the only method that resolves a truncated surname, a residence merged into a name, or an assentor list whose columns were interleaved.
scripts/ocr/crop-spn-region.py locates the notice on the page and renders it large enough to read. Each record below was read off that crop.

The FABRICATION FINDING is why this exists at all. docs/review/SPN-OCR-PROVENANCE.md reported that the LLM extraction 'did not invent this data', on the strength of a trace test that looked for any 4-character run of each surname in the source text. That test was too permissive and the conclusion was WRONG. Read directly, BL_0000038_19541123 carries exactly ONE candidate; the extraction has two, the second being a wholly fabricated 'McATEER, Edward' with a fabricated proposer, seconder and agent address. The trace test passed it because fragments of those strings occur elsewhere on a page of cattle-market advertising.

nominationStatusVocabulary.source: Column 6 of the statutory form: 'Decision of returning officer that nomination paper is invalid, or other reason why a person nominated no longer stands nominated'.

values.nominated: Column 6 blank. Validly nominated; went to a poll or was returned unopposed. Should join to a Civgraph candidate row.
values.withdrawn: No longer stands nominated. Never appeared on a ballot, so CANNOT appear in results-derived data. A failure to join is correct, not a defect.
values.invalid: The returning officer rejected the nomination paper. Likewise never on a ballot.

fieldNotes.assentors: The notice lists proposer, seconder and assentors in one column, in that order. The first two are recorded as proposer and seconder; the remainder as assentors. Where the form separates them into their own sub-columns (1962), that separation is used directly.
fieldNotes.description: The occupation or office printed in the 'Description' column. It is NOT the party. The 1954 extraction recorded 'Ulster Unionist' where the notice says 'Farmer'.
fieldNotes.outcome: Recorded only where the notice itself declares it, which the combined 'Statement of Persons Nominated and Declaration of Result' forms do for uncontested seats.

notices.title: Parliamentary Election for the Armagh Constituency
notices.formType: Statement of Persons Nominated and Declaration of Result
correctsExtraction: The extraction invented a second candidate, 'McATEER, Edward', with proposer 'Patrick J. O'Hare', seconder 'Patrick Agnew' and agent 'James O'Reilly'. NONE of these appear on the notice. The seat was uncontested with a single nominee.
Description was recorded as 'Ulster Unionist'; the notice says 'Farmer'.
Proposer was recorded as 'Robert J. Bell'; the notice says 'Frederick N. L. Bell'.
Agent address was recorded as '74, Scotch Street, Armagh'; the notice says '24 Windsor Avenue, Lurgan, Co. Armagh'.

notices.title: Northern Ireland Parliamentary Election, 1962
notices.formType: Statement of Persons Nominated and Declaration of Results of Uncontested Elections
correctsExtraction: 'O'NEILL, PHELEIM' — the notice reads Phelim Robert Hugh O'Neill.
Proposer recorded as 'Robert Hugh O'Neill.' — that is part of Phelim O'Neill's own forenames, read out of the adjacent column. His proposer was Arthur G. Algeo.
Proposer 'James S. M'Ilrath.' does not appear on this notice at all.
The extraction captured 3 of the 5 constituencies on this page.

notices.title: Parliamentary Election for the South Down Constituency
notices.formType: Statement of Persons Nominated and Notice of Poll
correctsExtraction: 'Lawrence Percy Ossory' was one of the 252 surnames Civgraph had never seen, and it is not a surname at all. The candidate is ORR, Lawrence Percy Story; 'Ossory' is the name of his HOUSE, read out of the Place of Residence column. He sat as UUP MP for South Down from 1950.

'MACGOUGAN, John' was recorded with proposer 'Michael Fay' and seconder 'Bernard Larkin'. The notice gives Michael Murphy as proposer and Bernard Larkin as seconder; Michael Fay is an assentor further down the list.
